title: What happens when variance is infinite

problemStatement.formal: \text{When } E[X^2] = \infty, \text{ normalized sums converge to an } \alpha\text{-stable distribution with characteristic function } \exp(-|t|^\alpha)
problemStatement.plain: When the variance of a distribution is infinite (power-law tails), the sum of n i.i.d. copies normalized by n^(1/α) converges to an α-stable distribution. The characteristic function exp(-|t|^α) satisfies the stability property [φ(t/n^(1/α))]^n = φ(t).
whyMatters: Explains convergence behavior for heavy-tailed distributions (finance, internet traffic, physics)
Completes the classification of all possible CLT limit distributions
Reveals the Gaussian as a special case (α=2), not the universal limit

proven: Main stability theorem: [φ_α(t/n^(1/α))]^n = φ_α(t) for all α > 0
Lévy distribution is 1/2-stable with normalization n²
Non-Gaussian stable laws (α<2) differ from Gaussian via log-injectivity
open: Full formalization of Gnedenko-Kolmogorov domain of attraction theorem (requires measure theory)
Lévy-Khintchine representation formal proof (requires Bochner's theorem)
knownResults.goal: Formal proof that infinite-variance distributions converge to α-stable laws

currentState.focus: All main theorems proved. Gnedenko-Kolmogorov and Lévy-Khintchine axiomatized.

insights: The key algebraic identity is |t/n^(1/α)|^α = |t|^α/n — this is why n^(1/α) is the right normalization
stableCharFun must be defined as Complex.exp(↑(-(|t|^α))) in Lean 4.26.0 (no HPow ℂ ℝ ℂ instance)
Distinctness from Gaussian proved via: exp equality → exponent equality → log equality → α=2 contradiction
Gaussian is special because 2^α < 2^2 for α < 2 (strict monotonicity of rpow)
Complex.exp_nat_mul gives (exp z)^n = exp(n*z) — key for stable_property proof
inv_mul_cancel₀ needed for α⁻¹ * α = 1 (Lean stores 1/α as α⁻¹)
